targetTest: an entry with an invalid asset ref never reaches the read port and is marked unavailable
expected: loadProjectBrushSet lists every well-formed tip of the pack, healthy or not: an unavailable tip keeps its entry with digest/mask null so the library can grey it (D-18), it is added to unavailableTipIds, and the failure carries the precise reason (missing / unreadable / wrong-size / digest-mismatch / refused for native results, invalid-asset-ref for a malformed or absent asset ref — never sent to the read port, batch-failed when the whole read is refused). Three failures collapse into ONE aggregate unavailable state naming three ids; the open never throws and no mask is ever fabricated.
actual: The RED run executed all 26 assertions across the two files: 6 new loader assertions fail while the 3 opening/source-order pins and the full 17-assertion catalog suite stay green. Task 1 healthy-only semantics surfaced exactly as expected: a refused batch listed 0 entries instead of 2 (expected [] to have a length of 2), a single failed entry listed 1 of 2, a digest mismatch listed 0 of 1, a valid record without an asset listed 0 of 1, the aggregate-three case listed 1 of 4, and the malformed-asset-ref id never reached unavailableTipIds (the id join came back empty string instead of wc/custom-bad). The round-fallback catalog pin passes already by construction because the registry absence alone yields the neutral preset — the production change is confined to listing and reason reporting.
semanticAssessment: The target test executed and failed on its planned assertion: "expected  " to be "wc/custom-bad"". Six loader tests failed and all other 20 assertions passed in the same run; no file failed to load or collect, and no failure is an import, syntax, setup or fixture fault. The failures are exactly the intended behavior gaps: loadProjectBrushSet drops unavailable tips from entries, omits their ids from unavailableTipIds (including malformed-asset-ref ids it never sends to the read port), and cannot yet represent a listed-but-unavailable tip. The catalog round-fallback pin is a regression guard for D-21/D-22, green at RED because it pins existing registry-absence behavior.
